::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Status:** starter entry, open for contributions. Not a LENS consensus. "Recoverability" is
used in several distinct senses; this page records them side by side.
:::

## Core question

Given the data and the model we have, which target quantities can be learned (recovered), even
when the model as a whole is not identifiable?

## Definitions across fields

### Missing data (graphical models)

> A target quantity (e.g. a joint distribution or a causal effect) is recoverable if it can be
> computed consistently from the distribution of the observed, partially missing data, given
> the assumptions encoded in a missingness graph (m-graph). [@mohan2013graphical]

### Causal inference: selection bias and data fusion

> A query is recoverable from selection-biased data if it can be computed from the distribution
> of the selected sample, possibly together with external unbiased data, under the assumptions
> in the causal graph. [@bareinboim2014recovering; @bareinboim2016causal]

### Inverse problems and compressed sensing

> "Recovery" of a signal refers to reconstructing it exactly or stably from incomplete
> measurements under structural conditions such as sparsity.
> [@candes2006robust]

### LENS working usage

> *(interpretation, not settled)* Recoverability asks which **functionals** of a
> non-identifiable or partially identified model can be learned. These may be identified
> functionals, functionals with informative bounds, or functionals whose posterior
> concentrates even though the full parameter's does not.

## Formal statement

*(no single formal definition; candidates below)*

- **Identified functional:** $\psi$ is recoverable if $P_{\theta_1} = P_{\theta_2} \Rightarrow
  \psi(\theta_1) = \psi(\theta_2)$. See [identifiability](identifiability.qmd).
- **Graphical recoverability:** $Q$ is recoverable if $Q(M_1) = Q(M_2)$ for every pair of models
  $M_1, M_2$ compatible with the graph that agree on the observed-data distribution.
  [@mohan2013graphical]
- **Bayesian learning** *(proposed)*: the posterior for $\psi$ differs from its prior, or
  concentrates, as $n \to \infty$. [@gustafson2015bayesian]

## Examples

- $Y \sim N(a + b, 1)$: $a + b$ is recoverable, $a$ is not.
- Recovering a population distribution from a selected sample when selection depends only on
  variables that are measured. [@bareinboim2014recovering]
- Exact recovery of a sparse signal from far fewer Fourier coefficients than the signal length.
  [@candes2006robust]

## Connections and distinctions

- **vs. [identifiability](identifiability.qmd):** in causal inference and missing-data work,
  "recoverable" and "identifiable" are close to synonyms; the difference is mainly the setting
  (missingness or selection). *(proposed; needs discussion)*
- **[Partial identification](partial-identification.qmd):** a functional constant over the
  identified set is recoverable. Others are recoverable only up to bounds.
- **[Practical identifiability](practical-identifiability.qmd):** a recoverable functional can
  still be estimated imprecisely.

## Key references

- @mohan2013graphical: recoverability with missing data.
- @bareinboim2014recovering and @bareinboim2016causal: recoverability from selection bias, and
  data fusion.
- @candes2006robust: "recovery" in compressed sensing.
- @gustafson2015bayesian: what is learnable in partially identified Bayesian models.

## Open questions

- *(open)* Should LENS adopt one definition of recoverability, or keep several labelled
  definitions (graphical, Bayesian, bound-based)?
- *(open)* How can recoverability be diagnosed in practice for complex hierarchical, spatial,
  or measurement-error models?
